function: Learned multi-hop RIS path scheduling (GNN) and joint BS active plus RIS passive beamforming (DDPG), maximizing sum achievable rate (p. 1).
system: Downlink mmWave 28 GHz; BS ULA with Nt antennas, users with Nr antennas, multiple passive reflecting RISs (URA, M elements, b-bit phase), blocked direct link (pp. 3, 10).
method: GNN (residual edge-graph attention encoder, attention decoder) trained with improved baseline REINFORCE; DDPG actor-critic with quantization-aware training; reinforcement learning, trained per RIS count (pp. 6-9, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Saleh-Valenzuela geometric channel, path loss from Akdeniz et al. [33]; 5000-20000 generated RIS-deployment instances for training, validation, test; no public or measured data (pp. 4, 10-11).
test_conditions: GNN trained and tested separately for each RIS count J=5-20 on instances from one region; DRL results swept over M, Nt, Pmax, phase bits; no unseen-condition test (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Path: Dijkstra, greedy, Gurobi optimum. Beamforming: AO with SCA (non-learned), DQN and DDQN (learned), single-RIS scheme (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Sum achievable rate, optimality gap of path length versus Gurobi, running time, convergence over training epochs (pp. 11-14).
complexity: Big-O orders of the GNN, DRL, and conventional Dijkstra plus AO analysed (pp. 9-10); CPU running time versus number of RISs in Fig. 5 (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "we utilize the Saleh-Valenzuela geometric channel"; p. 10: "Based on the parameter setting in [33]" gives only the path loss. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 11: "We generate 5000, 10000, 15000, and" instances for J = 5, 10, 15, 20, one dataset per case; p. 11: "future work could explore online training, domain adaptation". No test in an unseen scenario is reported.
q3_support: p. 13: "AO method proposed in [31] as the baseline" (non-learned); p. 13: "the DDPG significantly outperforms other comparison models" (DQN and DDQN on the same beamforming problem, sum rate in Fig. 6, p. 12).
q4_support: p. 9: "The complexity of the proposed two-stage algorithm primarily arises from the GNN and DRL components" and gives the Big-O orders; p. 12: "we compare the running time of different optimization schemes" (Fig. 5).
q5_support: p. 11: "The training, validation, and test datasets are generated from" a simulated 3D region. No code or data link, no public dataset, and no measured data appear in the paper.
notes: The path-loss parameters come from Akdeniz et al. [33] (a measurement-based 28 GHz model, not in the q1 list) and the small-scale channel is a custom Saleh-Valenzuela model, so q1 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. Path selection through cascaded RISs is treated as RIS configuration, not routing above the physical layer, because the DDPG stage learns BS precoder and RIS phase shifts. Fig. 6 (p. 12) plots sum rate of DDPG, DDQN, and DQN against an optimal bound, so q3 rests on a performance comparison.
